full_text_policy: titles and abstracts only; full text is not stored

two_stage_protocol.stage_1_function_first: Searched for a measured functional effect without naming BUB1B, so the candidate set is not pre-filtered by what is already known to touch this gene.
two_stage_protocol.stage_2_dependency_adjudication: Searched each surviving candidate together with BubR1/BUB1B. Naming the gene is correct here because this is no longer discovery. Absence of a known link is recorded as INDEPENDENCE_UNESTABLISHED, never as independence.

adjudication_outcome: No candidate is established as BubR1-independent for the function it would supply. CENP-E has a BubR1-independent route to the outer corona (PMID:38354735) while the mechanism by which it initiates congression is explicitly BubR1-dependent (PMID:41120314) — localisation is not function, which is the same distinction Y155C forces. The three bypass branches therefore hold named candidates with open dependency questions rather than grounded components.

full_text_adjudication.note: Full text and supplementary were retrieved for the five load-bearing papers under the licensed route and adjudicated at experiment and figure level. The texts are not stored here — this snapshot stays titles and abstracts only — so what is recorded is the verdict and the figure it rests on.

PMID:41120314.basis: Fig. 6f: CENP-E reactivation in BubR1-depleted cells did not trigger congression. Fig. 5c: Aurora B inhibition with both CENP-E activity and BubR1 absent blocked congression completely, so BubR1 is required independently of CENP-E recruitment and cannot be compensated by Aurora inhibition. Also shows KIF18A is dispensable for CENP-E-mediated congression initiation.

PMID:38354735.basis: Every BubR1 experiment is a localisation measurement — CENP-E intensity relative to CENP-C after BubR1, Dynein or ZW10 depletion. No alignment or congression readout in the BubR1-independent arm.

PMID:41218610.basis: BubR1 appears five times, all as a localisation marker in CENP-C mutant cells. No experiment places KIF18A in a BubR1-limited background.

PMID:39541344.basis: BubR1 appears zero times in 454 sentences. Adds a positive mechanistic argument — targeting poleward flux affects alignment independently of kinetochore attachment status — plus three mechanistically independent rescues (low-dose taxol, HAUS8 or NuMA codepletion) of misalignment, lagging chromosomes and micronuclei in human RPE-1 and OVKATE cells, and a stated predictor (antiparallel overlap length). The misalignment rescued was flux-driven, not attachment-driven.

PMID:30341343.basis: The disassembly pathways do not target BubR1 directly (Mad2 for TRIP13/p31comet, Cdc20 for APC15), but the substrate complex contains BubR1 and the arrest TRIP13 depletion causes was itself Mad2- and BubR1-dependent (Fig. 3b). The dual role is demonstrated in one system: interphase TRIP13 loss causes activation failure through loss of soluble O-Mad2 (half-time 1.4 h), while loss just before mitosis causes a dramatic exit delay. The authors frame it as a delicate counter-balance in which both loss and overexpression matter.

full_text_adjudication.unifying_finding: Every experiment across all five ran at BubR1-present or BubR1-absent. None ran at BubR1-limiting, which is this case's actual state, so every published dependency verdict concerns a different regime. That is why each dependency branch keeps an `unestablished` outcome rather than resolving on the published work.
full_text_adjudication.reason: Adjudication left two branches populated with named candidates, so broad discovery stays closed per instruction.

recursive_search_depths.depth_1: function-first discovery for alignment, activation, silencing
recursive_search_depths.depth_2: dependency adjudication of each surviving candidate
recursive_search_depths.depth_3: opened by the frontier audit, not by a plan: actuators for BubR1 abundance beyond the four interrogated (CHIP/STUB1, autophagy, HSP70/DNAJ), a mechanistic handle for arrest competence (MPS1 cascade) together with the toxicity of chronic activation, the causal-independence and surrogate questions behind the tumour-risk gate, and selective elimination of aneuploid cells — which became the F4 family
recursive_search_depths.rule_6_note: External search is recursive: each depth was reached because a branch hit a missing capability, not because a search phase was scheduled.
